description: A topical corticosteroid cream prepared by incorporating hydrocortisone powder into a cream base
clinicalUse: Treatment of inflammatory and pruritic dermatoses

prescriptionDetails.examplePrescription: Hydrocortisone 2.5% Cream, Make 30 g, Sig: Apply thin layer to affected area twice daily

ingredients.name: Dermabase or Aquaphor Natural Healing Ointment
ingredients.calculationShown: 30 g total - 0.75 g active = 29.25 g base

formulation.beyondUseDate: 30 days from preparation when stored at room temperature (20-25°C)

dosageCalculations.calculation: 30 g × (2.5 g hydrocortisone / 100 g cream) = 0.75 g hydrocortisone
30 g total - 0.75 g hydrocortisone = 29.25 g base

steps.description: Calibrate and tare the electronic balance

steps.notes: Use weighing boat; record actual weight if different

steps.description: Transfer hydrocortisone powder to ointment slab
Weigh approximately 29.25 g of cream base
steps.notes: Total final weight should be 30 g

steps.description: Using geometric dilution: Add equal amount of base (0.75 g) to the powder
steps.notes: This is the first dilution step (1:1 ratio)

steps.description: Mix thoroughly using spatula with levigation technique
steps.notes: Use firm pressure to ensure uniform mixing; no powder particles should be visible

steps.description: Add an amount of base equal to the mixture (approximately 1.5 g)
Continue adding base in portions equal to the current mixture amount
steps.notes: Repeat geometric dilution until all base is incorporated
Ensure completely uniform appearance and smooth texture
Should be approximately 30 g (allow ±0.1 g for loss during transfer)

steps.description: Transfer to ointment jar using spatula
steps.notes: Pack tightly to avoid air pockets

visualInspection.notes: No visible particles, lumps, or grittiness; uniform color throughout

weighingVerification.notes: Final weight verified and within acceptable range

uniformity.method: Visual inspection of small sample on spatula
uniformity.result: Uniform distribution of active ingredient confirmed
uniformity.notes: No white particles visible indicating undispersed drug

labeling.directions: Apply thin layer to affected area twice daily
labeling.storage: Store at room temperature (20-25°C). Avoid excessive heat.
warnings: Keep out of reach of children
Do not use on broken skin unless directed
auxiliaryLabels: DO NOT USE IF PREGNANT OR NURSING WITHOUT CONSULTING DOCTOR

safety.specialHandling: Corticosteroid - avoid skin contact; use gloves
safety.allergyConsiderations: Check for corticosteroid allergy or hypersensitivity

counselingPoints: Apply a thin layer to affected area only
Wash hands before and after application (unless treating hands)
Avoid contact with eyes, nose, and mouth
Do not cover with occlusive dressing unless directed by prescriber
Do not use on face, groin, or underarms unless specifically directed
May cause skin thinning with prolonged use
Contact prescriber if condition worsens or does not improve in 2 weeks
Do not use for longer than prescribed

stability.storageConditions: Room temperature (20-25°C), avoid excessive heat and freezing
stability.reference: USP <795> for nonsterile, water-containing preparations in semi-solid base
stability.notes: Hydrocortisone is relatively stable in cream bases at room temperature

references: Marriott JF. Pharmaceutical Compounding and Dispensing. 2nd ed. Chapter 7: Semi-solid Preparations
Allen LV. Standard Operating Procedures for Ointments/Creams/Gels
Trissel LA. Trissel's Stability of Compounded Formulations. 6th ed.

notes.geometricDilution: Geometric dilution is essential for uniformly distributing small amounts of potent drug throughout a large amount of base. Always start with equal parts of drug and base, then double the mixture size with each addition.
alternativeBases: White petrolatum USP (for ointment rather than cream)
notes.higherStrengths: For higher strengths (e.g., 5%), may use pre-made hydrocortisone 1% cream and calculate using alligation or dilution with additional active powder
notes.commercialAvailability: Hydrocortisone is available commercially in 0.5%, 1%, and 2.5% strengths. Compounding may be needed for custom strengths or alternative bases.

clinicalPearls: Low-potency corticosteroid appropriate for mild-moderate inflammation
Generally safe for short-term use on large body areas
May be used in pediatric patients under supervision
Inform patients about proper topical corticosteroid use to prevent complications
